method: count both-unseen evaluation keys under a real 20 percent drug holdout, 20 random holdouts per arena, no modelling
verdict: both arenas exceed the requirement, so the cross-dataset failures were not power failures

this_refutes_R169s_hypothesis.the_hypothesis: if those arenas had far fewer than 1600 usable combinations, their failure was the expected outcome on power grounds alone
this_refutes_R169s_hypothesis.outcome: refuted. PAIR averages 2296 both-unseen keys, 43 percent above the requirement, and still failed.
this_refutes_R169s_hypothesis.so: insufficient measurement count is ruled out as the explanation for C78 and C89

the_block_must_be_restated.old: cross-dataset replication is blocked by resource, meaning sample size
the_block_must_be_restated.new: cross-dataset replication is blocked by a different measurement regime: PAIR saturates at about 89 percent viability, and its readout is not the same observable as the GDSC synergy score
the_block_must_be_restated.why_this_is_favourable_to_the_claim: if the arenas had merely been too small, their failure would say nothing. Since they are large enough, the failure points at construct validity rather than precision.

an_incidental_number_worth_keeping.reading: even the home arena falls below 1600 on some holdout splits, so power on the headline is ample on average but not on every split
an_incidental_number_worth_keeping.consistency: R163 reported a mean evaluation set of 4457, consistent with the 3566 measured here under a slightly different holdout

limits: Only key counts were measured; no cross-dataset model was refitted.
The holdout fraction is fixed at 20 percent and was not swept.
Only two arenas were covered; the third was not located.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
